findings.message: checkout without persist-credentials: false — tokens may leak
findings.remediation: Use persist-credentials: false when checking out external/untrusted repositories.
findings.impact: Checkout without persist-credentials: false leaves GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config for any process to read.
findings.attack_vector: actions/checkout defaults to persist-credentials: true — token leaks via .git/config.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: uses obfuscation libraries or eval-like patterns with code generation
findings.remediation: Avoid obfuscation at install time; keep runtime code inspectable.
findings.impact: Obfuscation or minification tooling can conceal generated behavior from source review.
findings.attack_vector: Runtime or install-time code generation uses an obfuscation/minification package.

findings.message: uses eval() or new Function() to execute dynamically generated code
findings.remediation: Remove dynamic evaluation and use fixed allowlisted implementations.
findings.impact: Dynamic eval/Function allows execution of arbitrary injected code, bypassing all static defenses.
findings.attack_vector: User input or fetched data flows into eval()/new Function() without sanitization.

findings.message: disables TLS verification or references plaintext HTTP transport (4 occurrences in this file)

findings.message: constructs a regular expression from a non-literal value (possible ReDoS) (2 occurrences in this file)
findings.basis: OWASP Regular Expression Denial of Service Prevention
findings.remediation: Use bounded, allowlisted patterns and enforce input and execution limits for dynamic regular expressions.
findings.impact: An attacker-controlled regular expression can consume excessive CPU and deny service.
findings.attack_vector: A non-literal value is passed to RegExp without pattern or execution bounds.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: attempts path traversal with encoded or nested patterns (5 occurrences in this file)

findings.attack_vector: URL-encoded or nested traversal sequences — bypass naive path validation that only checks single ../.
